title: Tool calls in a row fold into one line
body:
`Transcript::entries` in `src/session.rs` holds one `Entry::Tool` per tool call, and the screen draws each call on its own line with a blank line after it. An edit adds a `+N -M` line under its call. A turn that makes nine calls in a row takes about eighteen rows, which pushes the conversation around it off the screen.

## Proposal

- A run is two or more `Entry::Tool` in a row. An agent reply, a person's message, a thought or a notice ends it. An `Entry::Permission` row inside a run stays in it.
- A run draws folded as one line: a status dot, the number of calls, the count of each kind, and the run's combined diff, with `▸` at the right. While a call in the run is in progress, the line also shows that call's title.
- A click on the line unfolds the run into the calls as they draw today, each still foldable on its own. A second click folds it again. The fold state is kept under the first call's id.
- The grouping happens at draw time, so a session loaded through `session/load` groups the same way and the session model does not change.
- A single call between other entries draws as it does today.
- A sub-agent's `agent` line counts as one call in its parent's run.

Jack settled that a thought ends a run and that runs start at two calls. He refines the folded line once a first version is on screen.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: A first version landed, uncommitted on `dev`. `tool_runs` in `src/ui.rs` finds each run of two or more `Entry::Tool`, with `Entry::Permission` rows kept inside and any other entry ending it. `build_transcript` draws a run's first row with `group_row`, which shows the status dot, `N tools`, the count of each kind, the summed `+A −D`, `· K failed`, the title of a call in progress and the `▸` or `▾` marker. A folded run skips its entries. The fold key is `group:<first call id>`, kept apart from the first call's own fold, and its fold area covers only the group row, so a click on an unfolded call still toggles that call. On `scenarios/readme/thread.json` at 80 × 28 the nine calls draw as `● 9 tools   read 4 · search 2 · edit 2 · run 1   +3 −2`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text: Jack reviewed the first version on screen. Changes he asked for: every call takes one line, with an edit`s `+N -M` on the call`s own line rather than a line under it. An unfolded group draws its calls indented under the group line, with no blank lines between them. Each kind of call gets its own icon and colour, and the kind`s name takes the icon`s colour: read `≡` blue, search `◎` cyan, edit `±` yellow, delete `⌫` orange, move `➜` blue, run `❯` magenta, fetch `↓` cyan, think `∴` muted, mode `◇` accent, agent and other `•` muted. The spinner replaces the icon while a call runs, and a red `✗` replaces it when the call fails. The group line colours each kind`s count the same way. Green stays out of the kinds because it means done. The ASCII stand-ins went to their own issue.
